'''Sug Woo Shin''' ({{Korean|hangul=신석우}}; born 1978) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] working in [[number theory]], [[automorphic forms]], and the [[Langlands program]].

==Education==
From 1994 to 1996 when he was in Seoul Science High School, Shin won two gold medals (including a perfect score in 1995) and one bronze medal while representing South Korea at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=1060 |website=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]] |title=Sug Woo Shin |accessdate=March 10, 2021}}</ref>
He graduated from [[Seoul National University]] with a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics in 2000.<ref name="CV"/> He received his PhD in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 2007 under the supervision of [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=137202}}</ref>

==Career==
Shin was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2007 to 2008, a Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]] from 2008 to 2010, and again a member at the Institute for Advanced Study from 2010 to 2011.<ref name="CV"/> He was an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 2011 to 2014.<ref name="CV"/> In 2014, Shin moved to the Department of Mathematics at the University of California, Berkeley as an associate professor.<ref name="CV"/> In 2020, Shin became a full professor of mathematics at the University of California, Berkeley.<ref name="directory">{{cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/sug-woo-shin |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |title=Sug Woo Shin |access-date=December 30, 2020}}</ref>

Shin is a visiting KIAS scholar at the [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]] and a visiting associate member of the [[Pohang Mathematics Institute]].<ref name="CV"/>

==Research==
In 2011, [[Michael Harris (mathematician)|Michael Harris]]<ref>{{cite book |last=Harris |first=M. |chapter=An introduction to the stable trace formula |editor-first=L. |editor-last=Clozel |editor2-first=M. |editor2-last=Harris |editor3-first=J.-P. |editor3-last=Labesse |editor4-first=B. C. |editor4-last=Ngô |title=The stable trace formula, Shimura varieties, and arithmetic applications |volume=I: Stabilization of the trace formula |location=Boston |publisher=International Press |year=2011 |pages=3–47 |isbn=978-1-57146-227-5 }}</ref> and Shin<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shin |first=Sug Woo |year=2011 |title=Galois representations arising from some compact Shimura varieties |url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2011/173-3/p09 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series |language=en |volume=173 |issue=3 |pages=1645–1741 |doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.3.9 |issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free }}</ref> resolved the dependencies on improved forms of the [[Arthur–Selberg trace formula]] in the conditional proofs of generalizations of the [[Sato–Tate conjecture]] by Harris (for products of non-[[isogeny|isogenous]] [[elliptic curve]]s)<ref>Carayol's Bourbaki seminar of 17 June 2007</ref> and Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–[[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Taylor]] (for arbitrary non-[[Complex multiplication|CM]] holomorphic [[modular form]]s of weight greater than or equal to two).<ref>{{Cite journal

==Awards==
Shin received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Fellowship]] in 2013.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~swshin/CV.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae (Sug Woo Shin) |date=January 2021 |access-date=March 10, 2021}}</ref>

Shin received a [[Ho-Am Prize in Science|Samsung Ho-Am Prize]] in 2025<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.hoamfoundation.org/eng/award/thisyear.asp | title= HOAM Foundation | access-date=April 2, 2025}}</ref>  for his contributions to the Langlands Program.

He was elected to the 2026 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2026 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>
